stem: Which of the following tool calls would be classified as action tools with real, persistent side effects? (Select 2)

options.text: A tool that cancels a real subscription
A tool that reads and returns the content of a public webpage
A tool that transfers funds between two accounts
A tool that returns the current server timestamp

explanation.why_correct: Canceling a subscription and transferring funds both cause real, persistent changes to external systems -- the defining trait of action tools.

why_incorrect.B: Reading and returning webpage content is a read-only retrieval with no side effect on the webpage or any other system.
why_incorrect.D: Returning a timestamp is a pure information lookup with no side effect.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Action tools change real external state (cancellations, transfers); information tools only read and return data without changing anything.

stem: An agent needs to answer a question about a specific user's current private order status, which only exists in that company's internal system. Why can the model not reliably answer this from internal knowledge alone?

options.text: Order statuses are universal and identical for every user
This private, system-specific data could not have been part of the model's general training data
The model has memorized every company's private database by default
This type of question is always unanswerable regardless of tool access

explanation.why_correct: A specific user's private, system-internal order status is exactly the kind of system-specific private data that a general-purpose model's training data could never have contained, making a tool-based lookup against that system necessary.

why_incorrect.C: Models are not trained on arbitrary companies' private internal databases; this data is inherently inaccessible to general training.
why_incorrect.D: With appropriate tool access to the relevant internal system, this type of question becomes readily answerable; it is not inherently unanswerable.
why_incorrect.A: Order statuses are specific to each individual order and user, not universal or identical across users.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Private, system-specific data that was never part of general training data requires a tool-based lookup against the actual system that holds it.

stem: Which scenario best illustrates grounding working as intended?

options.text: An agent generates a plausible-sounding but entirely unverified claim
An agent states a fact with no reference to where the information came from
An agent refuses to answer any question involving facts
An agent states a current fact and cites the specific retrieved source it came from, allowing that source to be checked

explanation.why_correct: Citing the specific retrieved source behind a claim is exactly what grounding looks like in practice -- it gives the claim a traceable, checkable origin.

why_incorrect.B: Stating a fact with no reference to its origin is the definition of an ungrounded claim, the opposite of grounding working as intended.
why_incorrect.C: Refusing to answer any factual question entirely sidesteps the task rather than demonstrating grounding.
why_incorrect.A: An unverified, plausible-sounding claim with no traceable source is exactly the kind of ungrounded claim that risks hallucination.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Grounding in practice means citing a specific, checkable source behind a claim -- not omitting sources or generating unverified assertions.
